name: Agentic AI Threat Model
description: Lifecycle-wide threat modeling for autonomous systems, including tool use, skills, delegation, and runtime control boundaries.

tasks.name: Map agent system
tasks.objective: Inventory agents, models, users, identities, credentials, tools, skills, MCP/A2A endpoints, memory, retrieval stores, external content, data classes, network boundaries, human approvals, persistence, telemetry, and deployment environments.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every capability with side effects has an identity, privilege boundary, and caller path.

tasks.name: Define trust and control goals
tasks.objective: State assets, security/privacy goals, authorized agent objectives, forbidden actions, least-privilege expectations, approval boundaries, audit requirements, budget/rate limits, runtime kill/deny controls, and safe failure behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Security goals cover what agents may access, change, delegate, remember, spend, and disclose.

tasks.name: Elicit agentic threats
tasks.objective: Systematically enumerate prompt/goal hijacking, indirect injection, tool and skill misuse, privilege escalation, identity spoofing, memory/retrieval poisoning, sensitive-data leakage, unsafe delegation, resource/budget abuse, sandbox escape, compromised orchestration, insecure inter-agent communication, supply-chain compromise, and monitoring evasion. Map to current agentic-security frameworks where useful.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Threats are architecture-specific abuse paths, not copied vulnerability labels.

tasks.name: Build attack paths
tasks.objective: Connect entry vectors to agent reasoning, identity, tool/skill calls, data access, delegation, persistence, spend/resource effects, and consequences. Include multi-step chains and attacker-controlled content crossing trusted contexts.

acceptanceCriteria.description: High-impact threats identify concrete preconditions and reachable effects.

tasks.name: Design preventive and runtime controls
tasks.objective: Apply least privilege, scoped credentials, capability/skill allowlists, provenance, content isolation, explicit confirmation, policy middleware, sandboxing, egress controls, memory hygiene, signed metadata, rate/budget limits, audit logs, behavioral telemetry, anomaly detection, runtime deny/kill controls, and fail-closed behavior at the earliest effective boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each high-impact attack path has preventive, detective, containment, and recovery controls where feasible.

tasks.name: Adversarially validate controls
tasks.objective: Design safe red-team cases for prompt injection, poisoned retrieval, malicious tool output, skill tampering, credential abuse, confused deputy behavior, identity spoofing, delegation loops, resource exhaustion, memory persistence, and policy bypass. Verify telemetry shows what the agent attempted and why it was blocked or allowed.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Controls are tested against representative multi-step abuse paths.
Agent actions remain inspectable and attributable during tests.

tasks.name: Package residual risk
tasks.objective: Record validated controls, unresolved risks, assumptions, monitoring signals, incident playbooks, re-test triggers, control owners, and architecture changes that would invalidate the model.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Residual risk states what remains possible after controls, not merely what controls exist.
